query: What institution holds the legislative powers granted by the Constitution?
expected_answer: The legislative powers granted by the Constitution are vested in the United States Congress, which consists of a Senate and House of Representatives.
source_context: Article I, Section 1: All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.

query: How often are members of the House of Representatives chosen?
expected_answer: They are chosen every second year.
source_context: Article I, Section 2: The House of Representatives shall be composed of Members chosen every second Year by the People of the several States. Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States according to their respective Numbers.

query: How many senators does each state have under the original constitutional text?
expected_answer: Each state has two senators.
source_context: Article I, Section 3: The Senate of the United States shall be composed of two Senators from each State, chosen by the Legislature thereof, for six Years; and each Senator shall have one Vote.

query: How long is a senator's term according to the text?
expected_answer: A senator serves a six-year term.
source_context: Article I, Section 3: The Senate of the United States shall be composed of two Senators from each State, chosen by the Legislature thereof, for six Years; and each Senator shall have one Vote.

query: What happens to a bill after it passes both houses of Congress?
expected_answer: It is presented to the President, who may sign it or return it with objections.
source_context: Article I, Section 7: Every Bill which shall have passed the House of Representatives and the Senate shall, before it become a Law, be presented to the President of the United States. If he approve he shall sign it, but if not he shall return it, with his Objections.

query: How long is the President's constitutional term?
expected_answer: The President serves a four-year term.
source_context: Article II, Section 1: The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America. He shall hold his Office during the Term of four Years, and, together with the Vice President chosen for the same Term, be elected.

query: Where is the executive power vested?
expected_answer: The executive power is vested in the President of the United States.
source_context: Article II, Section 1: The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America. He shall hold his Office during the Term of four Years, and, together with the Vice President chosen for the same Term, be elected.

query: What courts does Article III establish or authorize?
expected_answer: It vests judicial power in one supreme Court and in inferior courts that Congress may establish.
source_context: Article III, Section 1: The judicial Power of the United States shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish. The Judges shall hold their Offices during good Behaviour.

query: How long do federal judges hold office under Article III?
expected_answer: They hold office during good Behaviour.
source_context: Article III, Section 1: The judicial Power of the United States shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish. The Judges shall hold their Offices during good Behaviour.

query: What does full faith and credit require states to give one another?
expected_answer: Each state must give full faith and credit to the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of every other state.
source_context: Article IV, Section 1: Full Faith and Credit shall be given in each State to the public Acts, Records, and judicial Proceedings of every other State.

query: What are the two constitutional routes for proposing an amendment?
expected_answer: Congress may propose one when two thirds of both Houses deem it necessary, or Congress may call a convention on applications from two thirds of the state legislatures.
source_context: Article V: The Congress, whenever two thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose Amendments to this Constitution; or, on the Application of the Legislatures of two thirds of the several States, shall call a Convention for proposing Amendments.

query: What does the Constitution call the supreme Law of the Land?
expected_answer: The Constitution, federal laws made pursuant to it, and treaties made under United States authority are the supreme Law of the Land.
source_context: Article VI: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land.

query: How many states had to ratify the Constitution for it to be established between ratifying states?
expected_answer: Nine states had to ratify it.
source_context: Article VII: The Ratification of the Conventions of nine States, shall be sufficient for the Establishment of this Constitution between the States so ratifying the Same.

query: Which freedoms are protected by the First Amendment?
expected_answer: It protects religious establishment and free exercise, speech, press, peaceful assembly, and petitioning the government for redress of grievances.
